newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Aug 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Although Sydney Kings and Townsville Suns are believed to be interested in Perth guard Aaron Trahair, the Wildcats expect to sign Trahair to a long-term contract within a week. Trahair missed Perth's win against Sydney last week because of an ankle injur, but will be fit to face Canberra and North Melbourne this weekend. Page 21.

Despite being involved in a three-horse pile-up at Wyong yesterday, champion jockey Mick Dittman will be fit to ride Caulfield Cup and Epsom Handicap favourite Filante in tomorrow's A$120,000 Chelmsford Stakes at Randwick. Dittman, two other jockeys and he three horses all avoided serious injury. Page 22.

Carlton president John Elliott last night threatened to take the Australian Football League to court if a rule preventing Carlton and Collingwood from entering teams in a national soccer competition was not rescinded by 1pm tomorrow. Page 22.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

2UE radio announcer Ray Hadley has slammed the ABC's decision to cancel its weekend coverage of rugby league, praising the talent of ABC rival Peter Wilkins and his team who consistently finish second behind the bigger-budgeted 2UE in the football ratings. Page 39.

A shortage of funds will force the ACT Brumbies to cut back the size of their squad and New South Wales to stop recruiting players from overseas or interstate next season. The three Australian-based Super 12 rugby union camps, Queensland, ACT and NSW, hav discovered that the 10-year pay TV deal between News Corporation and SANZAR has not been as lucrative as first anticipated. Page 39.

Suffering two groin strains, champion Sydney full-forward Tony Lockett is only 80 to 90 percent fit, according to Swans coach Rodney Eade. Still, he is expected to play in the first AFL final at the SCG tomorrow night against Hawthorn, even though he faled to participate in training last night. Page 40.
THE AGE

In an effort to encourage more Tests between India and Australia, the Indian and Australian Cricket Boards announced the introduction of the Border-Gavaskar Trophy, named in honour of the only two batsmen to have scored more than 10,000 Test run. The trophy will be presented for the first time to the winner of next month's one-off Test in New Delhi. Page C11.

Soccer Australia has dispensed with the need for prospective recruits to be officially transferred, clearing the way for Gippsland Falcons coach Frank Arok to try out four players from his former club, Port Melbourne, in the first-round National Cup matchagainst South Melbourne at Bob Jane Stadium tonight. Page C11.

The Bulleen Boomers hope to overcome the draining effects of a virus and playing four games in seven days in the past week to win against the Perth Breakers in the Women's National Basketball League semi-final this weekend. Page C12.
HERALD SUN

Melbourne-Waverley Puma coach Norma Plummer hopes to finish her final State league netball season on a winning note. Melbourne has won the league title six times in eight years and will face Kea in a grand-final clash at the Glasshouse tonight, before taing on its new identity, Phoenix, in next year's national netball league. Page 102.

The Sydney Swans have re-signed fullback Andrew Dunkley for three years, after he rejected an offer from new AFL club Port Adelaide. Sydney has also re-signed chief executive Kelvin Thompson and coach Rodney Eade, who lifted the Swans from 12th last yearto first this year. Page 108.

Essendon needs to beat the Bears in Brisbane tonight to be certain of staying in the battle for the AFL Premiership, but Bombers coach Kevin Sheedy will also be hoping for a win to help secure his coaching future. Wanting to continue as Essendon coach fo at least three more years, Sheedy needs a good performance to convince the board's Tim Watson supporters that he is the man for the job. Page 112.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Western Suburbs fullback Andrew Leeds will play with a broken bone in his ankle in tonight's quarter-final against Cronulla at Parramatta Stadium. Leeds will play with the aid of pain-killing injections, after doctors said the match would do no further damage. Page 108.

While she'll start swimming training again soon, dual Olympian Sam Riley has kicked off her TV career, signing with Fox Sports for promotional purposes and to learn the media ropes. Riley shot her first "to camera" pieces yesterday, appearing in five-minte segments for the Girl'zone program, encouraging teenage girls to embrace a healthier lifestyle. Page 110.

In a bid to counter Manly's aggressive game, Sydney City coach Phil Gould will dump captain Sean Garlick and top tryscorer Peter Clarke from Sunday's quarter-final with the Sea Eagles. Back-rower Shane Millard will play hooker, fullback Ivan Cleary will move to the centres and Brad Fittler will take up the five-eighth position. Page 112.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
